A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GUI-WORLD and GUI-VID. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model benchmarking, GUI-VID fine-tuning experiments, ablations and human validation of annotations and automated judging.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds downstream benchmark evaluations, a human preference study and further ablations.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline and GUI-VID procedure remain unchanged: two-stage fine-tuning of VideoChat2 using UMT-L, instruction-conditioned QFormer, LoRA and the same losses. UVD keyframe selectors are evaluated alternatives, not a documented replacement of the proposed model.

E1.justification: The original 12,379-video, six-scenario GUI-WORLD dataset and auxiliary training sources remain. v2 adds training and evaluation on Mind2Web-Multimodal for GUI-operation questions and evaluation on MVBench for general video understanding, substantially extending the task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds main comparisons labeled LLaVA-OV-7B and Video-LLaVA, and reports LLaVA-Next-Video-7B-DPO in Appendix D. UVD+VIP and UVD+R3M expand the keyframe comparisons. VideoLLaMA and VideoChatGPT participate in the new MVBench comparison. Some LLaVA labels and overlapping scores are not clearly reconciled.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot and three-epoch fine-tuned Mind2Web evaluations on test-domain and test-website subsets, and preference judgments by five annotators over 180 videos. v2 adds a no-vision control and removes BLEU/BERTScore evaluation reporting. Main Table 5 also pools previously separate sequential and prediction scores into a dynamic category.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation excluding MetaGUI and OmniAct, model-based keyframe comparisons, a no-vision control, cross-benchmark ranking analysis and human helpfulness judgments. MVBench examines retention of general video capabilities. Original image/video and frame-count ablations remain, while appendix case studies are substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing human-versus-LLM-judge correlation analysis is retained unchanged. New preference percentages and benchmark rankings do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Most original appendix scores remain, including GUI-VID's overall 54.6% MCQA and 2.796 free-form scores. New results include fine-tuned Mind2Web test-domain accuracy of 25.14% versus 22.37% for VideoChat2, and MVBench averages of 41.1 versus 47.1, respectively. Numerous baseline, keyframe, preference and ablation results are added; six BLEU/BERTScore tables are removed.

T1.justification: The SFT and vision-grounded text-generation objectives retain the same mathematical content. No substantive definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central dataset contribution and claimed fine-tuning benefits remain. v2 reframes GUI-VID from a novel GUI agent/video agent toward an exploratory GUI-oriented assistant, narrowing the model's contribution framing while emphasizing benchmarking and understanding.

C2.justification: v2 argues that automated keyframe selection can substitute for manual selection, connects understanding with operational performance and user helpfulness, and discusses catastrophic forgetting on MVBench. It revises the interpretation of static versus dynamic strengths after regrouping scores. v1's explicit unseen-environment and computational-resource limitations are removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a 10,702/1,677 train-test split, adds an annotation metadata example and clarifies video-recording assignments. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of a changed split or collection procedure. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameters, hardware information, prompts and project access information largely remain.

R1.justification: Table 1 adds Screen2Words, Spotlight and GUICourse; references expand to newer LLaVA models and UVD/VIP/R3M. Several background and metric references are removed. The overall positioning relative to prior GUI datasets and models remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: v1's method-before-experiments narrative becomes benchmark analysis followed by exploratory model development and its experiments. Contributions and several results discussions are reorganized or rewritten, question examples move to the appendix, and standalone limitations and societal-impact sections disappear. The title and conference formatting also change.

P2.justification: Overall comparison tables are split and reorganized, task columns are merged, and numerous evaluation tables replace removed metric tables. Application lists give way to annotation metadata and distribution charts. Figures are relocated or redrawn; v2 Figures 6, 16 and 17 reuse an identical plot under three different model captions.

improvement.justification: New transfer tests, the external-data ablation and human study strengthen assessment of practical relevance and dataset-specific benefits; MVBench also exposes forgetting. However, v2 introduces duplicated plots for different models, preference percentages totaling 104% in Table 17, and prose calling UVD+VIP optimal despite Table 6 favoring UVD+R3M. Alongside removed supplementary metrics and limitations, these reporting problems make the net balance between stronger validation and reduced reliability uncertain.
